_meta.principle: Image editing uses fundamentally different prompt grammar from generation. Generation describes what to create; editing describes what to PRESERVE and what to CHANGE. FLUX Kontext, GPT Image 2 i2i, and NB2 image-edit all favor preserve/change clauses, identity markers, and stepwise edits over free-form rewrites.
sources: Black Forest Labs FLUX Kontext prompting guide (preservation clauses, stepwise edits)
OpenAI GPT Image 2 image-edit guide (natural-language edit instructions)
NB Pro multi-image composition docs (@img1 reference + edit-on-reference)
Adrian's Puck v3 lesson: prose drifts product details; use refs + preservation clauses
_meta.interpolation_rule: Editing prompts compose differently from generation prompts. Composer must detect edit intent (presence of `image_urls` + edit endpoint) and switch to editing.json templates instead of aesthetics.json.

preserve_change.name: Preserve / Change (FLUX Kontext canonical)
preserve_change.use: Default editing pattern. Describe what stays exactly the same, then what changes. Works on FLUX Kontext, GPT Image 2 i2i, NB2 image-edit. Most reliable edit pattern across models.
preserve_change.fragment: PRESERVE EXACTLY: [list what must NOT change — face, clothing, product, text, composition, lighting]. CHANGE ONLY: [list the single specific change — background, color, expression, pose].
negative_constraints: do not redraw the entire image
do not invent new details outside the change instruction
do not modify the preserved elements

flux-2-pro.syntax: exact preserve/change clauses; FLUX Kontext is purpose-built for this

nano-banana-pro.endpoint: POST /api/v1/nanobanana/edit-2 (or generate-2 with image_urls + edit instruction)

gpt-image-2.syntax: natural-language: 'change only the background to X, keep everything else exactly as in the reference'

imagen-4-standard.endpoint: Imagen edit endpoint (when available on WaveSpeed)
imagen-4-standard.syntax: describe target state + reference; Imagen weights edit refs loosely

identity_marker.name: Identity-marker preservation (face / hands / text)
identity_marker.use: When the identity-critical elements (face, hands holding the product, brand text, license key digits) MUST stay pixel-perfect. Use markers to be explicit.
identity_marker.fragment: [IDENTITY-LOCKED ELEMENTS — do not modify]: face, hands, product, visible text. [EDITABLE ELEMENTS]: [what can change]. The locked elements must match the reference image at pixel level.
negative_constraints: do not modify locked identity elements
do not redraw face or hands
do not regenerate text — preserve every character exactly

nano-banana-pro.syntax: @img1 + identity markers; NB2 is strongest at face/hand/text preservation

gpt-image-2.syntax: 'preserve identity exactly: face, hands, text. modify only: background.'

stepwise_edit_chain.name: Stepwise edit chain (multi-pass)
stepwise_edit_chain.use: When a single edit prompt would conflict with itself (change A, change B, change C all at once). Run as a chain — each pass changes ONE thing, output of pass N becomes input to pass N+1. FLUX Kontext docs explicitly recommend this for complex edits.
stepwise_edit_chain.fragment: Edit pass 1 of N: PRESERVE all original elements. CHANGE ONLY [single specific thing]. Pass output becomes input to pass 2.
negative_constraints: do not attempt multiple edits in one pass
do not deviate from the single specified change

flux-2-pro.syntax: chain N kontext calls, each with one preserve/change pair

gpt-image-2.syntax: chain N edit calls; GPT Image 2 token cost scales — keep passes minimal

background_swap.name: Background swap (subject-locked)
background_swap.use: Common product / portrait edit. Subject stays exactly. Background changes. Single most-used edit pattern in marketing image work.
background_swap.fragment: PRESERVE EXACTLY: the subject (product or person), all subject details, lighting on the subject. CHANGE ONLY: the background, replace with [new background description]. The subject's lighting must remain consistent with the original.
negative_constraints: do not modify the subject's edges or shadows

gpt-image-2.syntax: 'change only the background to X, keep the subject and its lighting unchanged'

color_grade_only.name: Color grade only (LUT-style)
color_grade_only.use: Apply a film/look/mood color grade without changing content. Useful for matching brand palette across a batch (DD copper warm, RH muted earth, TS toxic-green neon).
color_grade_only.fragment: PRESERVE EXACTLY: every visual element, composition, lighting direction, all subjects and backgrounds. CHANGE ONLY: the color grade — apply [target palette description]. Treat as a LUT pass, not a redesign.
negative_constraints: do not modify any element shapes or positions
do not change lighting direction — only color temperature/saturation

gpt-image-2.syntax: 'apply only a color-grade pass: [target palette]. preserve every other element'

object_remove.name: Object removal (inpaint-style)
object_remove.use: Remove a specific element — watermark, person in background, distracting prop. Inpaint-style edit.
object_remove.fragment: PRESERVE EXACTLY: the entire image. REMOVE: [specific element being deleted] and replace with plausible content from the surrounding context (matching texture, color, lighting).
negative_constraints: do not modify any element other than the removed object's region
